title: Queen’s Edict: Gifts of Karuvaki
excerpt: Ashoka orders donations by Queen Karuvaki to be recorded in her name.
html:
About this edict

The queen’s edict on the Allahabad–Kauśāmbī pillar names Karuvaki as the mother of Tivala. It is a rare inscription that identifies a Mauryan royal woman by name.

Original script

Roman transliteration

The text below follows the Allahabad–Kauśāmbī version in Hultzsch’s edition. Square brackets show restored or uncertain letters; dots mark damaged or missing text. Other surviving copies can differ.

(A) 1 Devānāṃpiyaṣā v[a]canenā savata mahamatā 2 vataviyā (B) e hetā dutiyāye devīye dāne 3 aṃba-vaḍikā vā ālame va dāna-[gah]e [va e vā pi a]ṃne 4 kīchi ganīyati tāye deviye ṣe nāni (C) [he]vaṃ .. [na] .. 5 dutīyaye deviye ti Tīvala-mātu Kāluvākiye

English translation

This is E. Hultzsch’s 1925 translation of the same version. Its terminology and bracketed restorations reflect that historical edition.

(A) At the word of Devānaṃpriya, the Mahāmātras everywhere have to be told (this). (B) What gifts (have been made) here by the second queen, (viz.) either mango groves, or gardens, or alms-houses, or whatever else, these (shall) be registered (in the name) of that queen. (C) This (is) [the request] of the second queen, the mother of Tīvala, the Kaluvākī.

Sources

  • E. Hultzsch, Inscriptions of Asoka (1925), Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, volume I.
  • Bibliotheca Polyglotta edition, University of Oslo (Magadhi transliteration, English translation, and inscription facsimiles).
